title: Flat index, split market: transpacific climbs as Asia–Europe slides
seoTitle: Container Rates Diverge: Transpacific Up, Asia–Europe Down
metaDescription: Drewry's World Container Index held flat at $4,465 on 3 September 2026 while transpacific rates rose and Asia–Europe fell sharply. What drove the split and what it means for quoting.
author: market
dek: Drewry's composite index did not move last week. Underneath it, transpacific rates set fresh highs while Shanghai–Genoa fell 10% — the clearest case this year for reading corridors rather than composites.
sources: Drewry World Container Index, assessment for 3 September 2026, and Drewry Container Capacity Insight.
FreightWaves, “Trans-Pacific spot rates reach new highs on resilient demand, port congestion”, 2 September 2026, citing Freightos data and analyst Judah Levine.

title: Panama Canal cuts daily transit slots as watershed rainfall disappoints
seoTitle: Panama Canal Cuts Daily Transit Slots, September 2026
metaDescription: From 3 September 2026 the Panama Canal cut Neopanamax slots to nine a day and Panamax to 25, falling to 23 on 15 September. The deeper draft cut was postponed to 1 October. What it means for canal-routed cargo.
author: research
dek: The Authority has switched from limiting how deep ships load to limiting how many transit at all. For Asia–US East Coast services routed through the canal, that is the more consequential lever.
sources: Panama Canal Authority, Advisory to Shipping of 20 August 2026 (transit capacity and draft postponements) and of 28 August 2026 (booking system modifications).
Panama Canal Authority, advisory of 5 August 2026 on Neopanamax draft limits, as reported by GAC Hot Port News, 7 August 2026.
DTN Progressive Farmer, “Panama Canal Authority Adopts New Transit Restrictions”, 2 September 2026.
FreightWaves, 31 August and 2 September 2026, on the record auction price and prospective low-water surcharges.

title: Seventeen rate increases in eight months: reading the transpacific GRI cadence
seoTitle: 17 GRIs in 2026: What the Transpacific Cadence Tells You
metaDescription: The 1 September general rate increase held on both US coasts — the seventeenth on the East Asia to USA lane this year, against roughly six in a normal year. What that frequency actually signals.
keywords: East Asia to USA rate increase
author: market
dek: An increase that sticks does not need repeating a fortnight later. The frequency, not the level, is what the transpacific is telling you — and the exposure it creates is about quote validity.
sources: Alba, “Market update — September 2026”, on the 1 September general rate increase and the count of increases year to date.
Drewry World Container Index, assessment for 3 September 2026, and Drewry Container Capacity Insight.
FreightWaves, 2 September 2026, citing Freightos rate data.
